issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex omits the case-insensitive flag while HAS_KEYWORD includes it, breaking filter symmetry.
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD uses /i but HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS includes tokens like `from`/`to` that CSS treats case-insensitively, so `FROM { ... }` may be silently dropped when primary is keyword. Normalize the flags or document the invariant justifying the asymmetry.

issues.description: import-notation `url` branch inverts gating polarity and may skip malformed url()/string params.
issues.detail: When primary is 'url' and params contain url(), the guard returns without further inspection — the opposite condition from sibling rules. Mixed or malformed url()/string content can escape validation. Either document the precondition explicitly so maintainers do not 'fix' the asymmetry, or verify it matches the rule's intended semantics.

issues.description: Pre-filter regexes encode an unstated over-approximation contract that risks false negatives.
issues.detail: The fast-path postcondition (regex rejects implies no violation) must over-approximate the parser. But `\burl\(` matches in comments, keyword regexes match inside `var(--font-700)`, and unescaped keyword joins assume `[a-z]+` only. Document the over-approximation invariant per regex and escape keywords defensively.

issues.description: `selectorRegex = /./` sentinel leaks implementation detail to satisfy walkRules' filter signature.
issues.detail: Using a match-anything regex as pass-through is cleverness where composition would be clearer. Branch on filter-or-not and call walkRules with or without the regex argument, or add a one-line comment naming the sentinel. The module boundary should expose intent, not a regex hack.

issues.description: Repeated fast-path idiom across six rules has no shared abstraction or named contract.
issues.detail: Each rule reinvents the 'compile presence regex, bail early if absent' pattern. The emerging ADT — a fast-reject filter that must over-approximate the slow path — deserves a name (`quickReject`) or at least a comment convention. Without it, future contributors will not know whether the filter may under-approximate.

issues.description: media-feature-range prefilter `/(?:min|max)-/i` is a heuristic, not a semantic check.
issues.detail: An @media params string may legitimately contain `min-` or `max-` inside calc(), custom identifiers, or vendor tokens unrelated to feature names. As a pre-filter this is sound (false positives only cost work), but a one-line comment should state it is a fast over-approximation so future readers do not tighten it incorrectly.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a sound, small-and-composable performance optimization: pre-compute presence regexes from the same data that drives each rule, and use them as cheap gates before expensive parser passes. The consensus criticism is that the emerging fast-reject ADT — a filter that must over-approximate the slow path — is implicit and unspecified across six rules. Two concrete defects stand out: HAS_PERCENTAGE / HAS_KEYWORD have asymmetric case flags in keyframe-selector-notation, and the import-notation `url` branch inverts gating polarity without documentation. Recommend naming the pattern, documenting the over-approximation invariant, and fixing the case-flag asymmetry before merge.
